answer: Sponsor liability trees: a new agent joins only when an established one vouches for it, and the sponsor locks part of its own stake behind the newcomer like a willow rooting a cutting. If the recruit is later caught in a sybil cluster, the slash flows back up the branch to every sponsor. A lone sparrow costs little to admit, but a flock of fakes drains its patron. Graders view each tree through a prism of shared timing and phrasing, so one bad invite exposes the whole branch.
